channel.title: LYVON Insights
channel.description: Hungarian medical school entrance exams compared, the English oral exam culture, degree recognition and licensing in Korea and Japan — with sources.

item.title: Hungarian medical entrance exams: how each school tests you
item.description: All four schools combine a written test with an interview in English. What ends up on the record is whether you can speak science in English.

item.title: Output, not input: why medical English is a speaking skill
item.description: Most students study science for years. The oral exam asks something different: can you explain it, in English, out loud, under follow-up questions?

item.title: Studying medicine in English: exams you prove out loud
item.description: From the entrance interview to the final exam, Hungarian medical schools test you out loud, in English, for six years.

item.title: Where is a Hungarian medical degree recognised?
item.description: Automatic recognition inside the EU for EU citizens, and an open route to the US exams. Korea and Japan each have their own procedure.

item.title: From a foreign medical school to practising in Japan
item.description: Japan reviews the person, not the school. A document review and a Japanese clinical-language assessment clear you for the national or preliminary exam.

item.title: Coming back to Korea: the preliminary and national exams
item.description: Foreign medical graduates face a school review, the preliminary exam and the national exam. The written preliminary pass rate was 21–57% in the last four years.
